runs.name: Starbucks Corporation
runs.entry: Price **$90.75** (close 2026-10-09, aggregator, flagged) x **1,140.0M shares** (10-Q cover, 0000829224-26-000130; one class; balance sheet 1,139.8M issued and outstanding, repurchased shares retired; no repurchases in FY2025 or FY2026 to date) = cap **$103,455M**; sovereign **5.60%** (UST 30Y par, 2026-10-09). Q1 IN (the roaster and retailer of specialty coffee in 89 markets, company-operated and licensed stores, the Nestle Global Coffee Alliance) · Q2 IN (North America decides, 70.1% of five-year segment operating income; its margin 24.2% FY2015, 19.8% FY2024, 11.5% FY2025, 11.8% for three quarters of FY2026; comparable transactions -5% FY2024, -4% FY2025, +3.9% for three quarters of FY2026; a notch lost through pricing past the customer and labour cost the field shares: McDonald's US company-operated margin 16.0% to 11.6% 2017 to 2025, Tim Hortons segment 33.6% to 25.4% 2019 to 2025, Dutch Bros 9.8% and Luckin 10.3% operating margins; Costa and private chains not filers; 60% of China retail sold to Boyu Capital, closed 2026-03-30, $4B enterprise value) · Q3 weighs against (high returns on store capital, a decade of added capital bought no growth in owner cash) · Q4 weighs against, no STOP (restructuring recurs; guidance and non-GAAP featured; FY2025 operating cash $4,747.5M cross-checked against the filed statement) · Q5 integrity IN (no restatement, enforcement or auditor change; the reports give traffic and the bad news), ability weighs for thinly; CEO pay $95.8M FY2024, mostly make-whole grants, $31.0M FY2025, bonus at 54.8% of target; the $250,000 aircraft limit replaced by a quarterly review in September 2025 · Q6 weighs against ($49.6B of dividends and buybacks FY2016 to FY2025, about 155% of $32.0B of earnings; buybacks at about $55 to $110, every price above the range's bottom; equity from +$5.45B FY2017 to -$8.1B FY2025, funded by Nestle's roughly $7B prepaid royalty and debt) · **Q7 OUT, the floor: owner cash (operating cash less stock pay, all capital spending and acquisitions, plus businesses sold, after-tax interest added back) cycle base 3,560 a year on specific (a), both end years of the literal window FY2021 to FY2025 aberrational on the filer's description (pandemic recovery with $1,175M from the Korea divestiture; the FY2025 restructuring); growth between the cycle averages FY2016 to FY2020 and FY2021 to FY2025 8.5% a year; net debt $9,355.1M at 2026-06-28; central range $45.46 to $99.49 all-equity ($50.71 to $94.95 equity-only), width 2.19, the price inside the range; returns about 6.0% on the growth case and 3.1% on the no-growth case at the price; 16.8% growth for ten years needed to earn the floor; literal window $11.52 to $45.46; fair $33.48 all-equity, $38.74 equity-only (literal window $12.49 and $20.21).** Q8 to Q12 not reached. Conventions of the run, confessed: the two five-year cycles; the Nestle prepayment removed from FY2018 operating cash (the variant that keeps it shown); 60% of the China enterprise value ($2.4B) deducted as the value given. Run by an earlier session, killed after Q4 (14213758); resumed by the overnight cycle of 2026-10-11 with one dispatched analyst (Q5 315ba74b, Q6 d05ab82a, Q7 39c5e19f, close 4b8b5f6c); the run file keeps its date of 2026-10-10 and the price and rate of that day, not refreshed (the analyst: the result is not close to either). The dispatcher re-checked: check_framework PASS; the dispatcher's dispatcher_quote_check.py 71 fragments, 0 problems, no E-ids; no tracked research file over 200 KB. Framework points for the operator (from the run): specific (a) asks for a cycle peak to peak while this filer names disrupted years, never a peak; a poor year inside a cycle average (the pandemic year, 181) lifts the growth between cycles, which specific (a) does not guard and which contradicts Q3's finding; the range convention caps growth by Q3's arithmetic, but Q3 is a weighing with no number; specific (f)'s share-of-sales cap does not say which sales; specific (c) has no rule for the partial sale of a business whose cash is in the base; a prepaid royalty in operating cash fits no specific; Q5's employee-conduct row reaches no filed source here (the labour board's record is not an SEC filing). Strongest other evidence against: the dividend (about $2.83B a year) exceeds FY2025 owner cash; operating leases about $12.4B undiscounted; debt $13.3B at June 2026. Could not get: the labour board's decisions; China's owner cash on its own; a maintenance capital figure; the CEO's record at his former employer. Position note filled at the fold: not held. The v4.1 bands retired.
runs.narr: A roaster and retailer of specialty coffee in 89 markets, whose North American margin halved from FY2015 to FY2025 as it priced past its customer and paid more for labour, with traffic returning in FY2026; the castle stands a notch lower. Paid out about 155% of a decade's earnings in dividends and buybacks, equity now negative. Priced inside a range whose top rests on growth measured from a pandemic-year base; no case earns the floor at $90.75.
runs.fair_label: SBUX at/below $33.48: the fair price on the all-equity basis of the blind v5 purchase run of 2026-10-10 (Test Runs/2026-10-10 Run - SBUX Starbucks.md; OUT at Q7 at $90.75; $38.74 equity-only; $12.49 on the literal window). A prompt to re-run Q7, never a verdict.
